name: Intuneomator
description: Intuneomator is a macOS enterprise tool that automates Microsoft Intune app lifecycle management, leveraging Installomator’s 900+ label database for multi-arch apps. It enables end-to-end workflows (download, package, upload, deploy), group targeting, metadata and script automation, plus Teams-based status and CVE alerts. Built with a secure XPC architecture, keychain-backed credentials, and dual authentication for enterprise-grade security.
keywords: how to automate mac app uploads
author: Gil Burns

securityCheck.aiSummary: The Intuneomator codebase shows legitimate automation patterns but contains notable security considerations. Key issues: (1) eval usage to parse label data introduces local code execution risk dependent on label integrity; (2) storing a complex build-script snippet as a string for project modification may obscure behavior and hinder auditing; (3) hardcoding a signing identity constitutes a credential-like exposure risk. Recommendations: replace eval with strict, explicit parsing of label contents; avoid embedding large scripts as strings in code paths; move signing identities/certificates to secure CI/CD secret stores or environment-managed credentials with proper access controls; add input validation and code reviews for all dynamic label data to prevent injection attacks.

noObfuscatedCode.reason: Usage of eval to load label values: eval 'case "$label" in '"$labelFile"'; esac' reads the entire label file content into shell variables. This creates a local code execution risk if a label file is tampered with or crafted to inject shell commands. It relies on the integrity of external label data and can be exploited to run arbitrary commands during label processing.
